decisions.evidence: Read all nine proof steps and the fourteen cited dependency statements. The positive-base chain rule gives f prime=1/2(1-z)^(-3/2) and f double prime=3/4(1-z)^(-5/2). Monotonicity and Taylor n=1 give K=3/8(1-z0)^(-5/2); endpoint continuity follows from the cited positive-base power continuity. z=0 and z0=0 give R=0. The denominator 1/2+K z0 is positive. Step 8.1 uses zN=1-N^(-2), f(zN)=N and N>B+3/2, genuinely disproving a global bound; divergence of the chosen upper bound alone would not do so. Lebl Section 4.3 Theorem 4.3.2 and its complete Rolle proof, and MIT Lecture 17 p.1 support the Taylor use. No AC or physical premise. Reader repair accepted; refuter has no finding.

Read the complete definition and all eight direct supplier definitions. S=span(e1,e2,e3)=e0-perp has positive definite delta; real scalar multiplication, supplied by def-vector-space, makes Np=mw an element of S, while NK=m delta(w,w)/2 is real. At w=0 both vanish. Coordinate derivatives are assigned only at differentiability points (hence limit points); empty and singleton intervals assign no undefined derivatives. Units are kg m/s and J, m>0 is input, and no physical approximation or measurement is asserted. Crowell pp.86,91,96,116 and Carroll p.27 supply motivation only. Reader repair accepted; no AC. Contract review additionally found falsely excluded empty/singleton intervals in the empty and degenerate rows. Corrected both to checked with exact empty differentiability-domain consequences; the already sound Definition and all item bytes are unchanged.

The positive base C>|v| handles nonzero v, and v=0 is separately identity. Substitution beta=v/c yields the passive boost. Independently read the complete boost lemma: its two-dimensional block preserves eta, has determinant +1 and inverse B(-beta), and preserves the future component. Thus e prime_a=B inverse e_a is an inertial frame with chart E inverse B(p-o). This closes the reader well-definedness repair. The final shorthand about unbounded regions is read through the exact cited whole-domain statement, not as a claim about every unbounded subset. No empirical assertion or AC.

Exact subtraction gives spatial error (gamma-1)(x_parallel-tv); Cauchy-Schwarz gives |x_parallel|<=|x|, with v=0 separately identity. Supremum exists on nonempty bounded D; the epsilon/2 specialization yields the usual strict convergence criterion. On the whole domain fixed nonzero v has positive error slopes along the displayed rays; on the unbounded perpendicular slice both errors vanish. Quantifiers and title correctly distinguish these. C varies as an auxiliary mathematical parameter, not the adopted physical c. Reader scope repair accepted; no choice or empirical assertion.

Read all seven counterexample steps and thirteen direct suppliers. Fixed future unit n and unit e exist in a nonempty three-dimensional positive rest space. For N>=2, |wN|^2=c^2(1-N^(-2))<c^2 and the entire segment n+s wN/c is timelike, hence its endpoint is in the future component; multiplying by positive cN preserves future direction. Pairing gives gamma=N, projection gives precisely wN, and eta(UN,UN)=-c^2. Absolute error is mc^2(N-3/2+1/(2N^2))>mc^2(N-3/2)>0. The ratio factors as (N-1)(2N+1)/(N+1)>=N-1. Archimedean N>max(2,B/(mc^2)+3/2) disproves every absolute B for fixed positive c,m and one n; N>M+1 separately gives relative divergence. No division at N=1 or w=0 occurs. No AC or empirical assertion; reader future-direction/sign repairs accepted.

Read all ten proof steps and thirteen direct dependencies, including postulate (i),(ii), the precise C1 future-timelike worldline definition, observer decomposition (e), and four-momentum lemma (b) with its derivation 1.2/2.2.
